en.headline: Parking meter system fails across Hong Kong, police hold off enforcement
en.dek: Transport Department says emergency repairs are under way after the operator reported a malfunction at 8.20am; Secretary Mable Chan says police will not ticket roadside spaces until fixed.
body: Hong Kong’s on-street parking meter system suffered a widespread malfunction on Tuesday morning, leaving many units displaying “out of order” while emergency repairs continued.

The Transport Department said it received a report from the operator, Hong Kong Telecom, at about 8.20am. It instructed the operator to carry out repairs as soon as possible, investigate the cause thoroughly and submit a report. A service hotline is available at 2332 3700.

Secretary for Transport and Logistics Mable Chan said the bureau took the incident seriously. Preliminary checks found no evidence of malicious interference. She confirmed that police would not enforce against vehicles parked at roadside metered spaces until the system was fully restored. Some meters had already resumed operation by late morning.
Drivers reported mixed conditions across districts, with some meters working normally and others still offline. Authorities expect an initial report from the operator within 24 hours.

zh.headline: 全港咪錶泊車系統故障 警方暫不執法路旁泊位
zh.dek: 運輸署接獲營運商早上約8時20分報告系統故障，正緊急搶修；陳美寶指未完全復修前警方不會就路旁咪錶位執法。
body: 全港路旁泊車咪錶系統周二早上出現故障，不少咪錶顯示「Out of order」，運輸署正進行緊急搶修。
運輸署表示，早上約8時20分接獲營運商香港電訊報告系統故障，已責成營運商盡快修復，徹查原因並提交報告。查詢熱線為2332 3700。
運輸及物流局局長陳美寶表示高度重視事件。初步調查未發現涉及惡意攻擊。她確認在系統未完全復修前，警方不會在路旁咪錶泊車位執法。部分咪錶至上午較後時間已恢復運作。
各區情況不一，有咪錶正常有咪錶故障。當局期望營運商在未來24小時內提交初步報告。
